questions.question: Which of the following is not an asexual form of reproduction in plants?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pollination.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Pollination is the** transfer of pollen from the male to the female part of a flower**, enabling** fertilization and seed production.**
 
• **Hence it is not an asexual form of reproduction.**
 
• It is vital for the** reproduction and survival **of flowering plants, resulting in the** formation of fruits and seeds.**
 
• Pollination occurs through **agents like wind, water, insects, birds, and animals, **depending on the plant's specific mechanisms and pollinator attraction.
 
• Pollinators, **such as bees, butterflies, birds, and mammals**, inadvertently transfer pollen while visiting flowers, facilitating the pollination process.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Vegetative Propagation**

 
 
• Vegetative propagation is a method of plant reproduction in which new individuals are formed from vegetative parts such as **stems, leaves, or roots, without the involvement of seeds.**
 
• It is an **asexual mode** of reproduction that allows plants to reproduce genetically identical offspring, maintaining the characteristics of the parent plant.
 
• Vegetative propagation can **occur naturally,** such as through the growth of plant **runners, rhizomes, or bulbs,** or it can be artificially induced through techniques like** cutting, grafting, or tissue culture.**
 
• This method of reproduction is commonly used in **horticulture and agriculture to propagate desirable plant traits, maintain consistency** in cultivated varieties, and rapidly multiply plants with desired characteristics.
 
 
 
• **Spore formation**
 
 
• Spore formation is a method of reproduction used by certain organisms, including** fungi, bacteria, algae, and some plants**, to produce offspring.
 
• Spores are** tiny, specialized structures that contain genetic material** and are capable of developing into new individuals under favourable conditions.
 
• The process of spore formation typically involves the formation and release of spores from the parent organism, which can then disperse through various means such as **wind, water, or animal transport.**
 
• Spore formation allows** organisms to reproduce and spread in environments** where other forms of reproduction, such as sexual reproduction or seed formation, may be challenging or less efficient.
 
 
 
• **Budding**
 
 
• Budding is a form of **asexual reproduction** where a new organism** develops as an outgrowth or bud from the parent organism.**
 
• The process of budding involves the formation of a **small bulge or bud **on the parent organism, which eventually grows and develops into a genetically identical individual.
 
• As the bud grows, it receives nourishment and genetic material from the parent organism until it reaches a certain size or maturity and detaches, becoming an independent organism.
 
• Budding is a common method of reproduction observed in various organisms, including **yeast, hydra, some plants, and even certain animals, **allowing for efficient and rapid population growth.

questions.question: The first cotton textile mill in Ahmedabad was started in which year?

__
 
• Ahmedabad's first cotton textile mill,** the Ahmedabad Cotton Mill,** started production on **May 30th, 1861.**
 
• It was founded by** Rao Bahadur Ranchhodlal Chhotalal,** an entrepreneur in **Ahmedabad.**** **
 
• It was a spinning factory with** 2,500 spindles** and employed **63 workers. **
 
• It catered to the local handloom weavers' yarn requirements.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The** first cotton textile mill in India **was established at** Fort Glastor near Kolkata in 1818.**
 
• **Large-scale production of cotton** started in **Mumbai in 1854.**
 
• **India's first successful mechanized textile mill** was instituted in the **city of Mumbai**, then known as Bombay, in the** year 1854.**
 
• There were several factors that led to the rapid expansion of the industry in the region, the region had **a warm, moist climate that was suitable for the industry.**

• The seventh schedule of the Indian constitution deals with the division of powers between the central government and the state governments through three lists: **the Union List, the State List, and the Concurrent List.**
 
• **The Union List **consists of subjects on which the central government has exclusive legislative authority.
 
• This means that only the** Parliament of India can make laws **regarding the items mentioned in the Union List.

questions.question: What is the colour of the outer zone of the complete combustion of a candle flame?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Blue.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **outer zone of complete combustion** in a candle flame is characterized by **blue colour. **
 
• This is due to the** presence of hot, oxygen-rich air **that allows for efficient burning of the candle's fuel.
 
• The blue colour indicates that the outer zone of the flame is at a **high temperature. **
 
• The complete combustion process in this zone ensures that the **maximum amount of fuel is oxidized, **resulting in the production of** heat and light.**
 
• The blue outer zone signifies that the combustion process is **producing minimal soot. Soot** is a black carbonaceous substance that is a **byproduct of incomplete combustion**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Yellow flame**

 
 
• The yellow flame is a** result of incomplete combustion**, where the **fuel does not burn completely** due to a **limited oxygen supply. **
 
• This incomplete combustion produces a yellow colour, indicating the presence of unburned carbon particles or other impurities in the flame.
 
• **Compared to a blue flame, a yellow flame is typically cooler.**
 
• The incomplete combustion process in the yellow flame** generates less heat and light **because not all of the fuel is being efficiently burned.
 
 
 
• **Orange flame**
 
 
• The orange flame is typically observed in the** intermediate zone of a candle flame,** which is** between the blue outer zone **of complete combustion and **the yellow inner zone** of incomplete combustion.
 
• The orange colour of the flame** indicates partial combustion **of the fuel. 
 
• It occurs when there is a **limited supply of oxygen**, resulting in the production of **carbon monoxide **and other partially burned fuel particles.
 
• The orange flame is** relatively cooler compared to the blue outer zone.**
 
• The orange flame **emits a moderate amount of light,** but it is not as bright as the blue flame. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.entrance360.com/media/uploads/2019/05/20/fire.png]

questions.question: Who is the implementing agency of “Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (ABDM)” ?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**NHA**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **National Health Authority (NHA)** is the implementing agency responsible for the **"Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (ABDM)"** in **India.** 
 
• The NHA oversees the** planning, development, and execution** of the mission, which** aims to digitize and transform healthcare delivery systems** in the country. 
 
• Through the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission, the NHA aims to establish a **robust digital health infrastructure, including the creation of a unique health ID** for every citizen, seamless data exchange, and the implementation of digital health records to enhance healthcare accessibility and quality across India. 
 
• The NHA plays a crucial role in driving the successful implementation of this transformative initiative.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **AIIMS**

 
 
• **All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS) **is a prestigious medical institute located in **New Delhi, India**.
 
• AIIMS was established in **1956. **
 
• It was established by an **Act of Parliament **and is an autonomous institution funded by the Indian government.
 
• It offers **undergraduate (MBBS), postgraduate, and doctoral programs **in various medical disciplines.
 
 
 
• **IMA**
 
 
• IMA is a **national voluntary organization **representing doctors in India.
 
• It was **founded in 1928 **and has a long-standing history in advocating for the **interests and welfare of the medical community**.
 
• It strives to uphold high standards of medical ethics, promote professional competence, and work towards the overall advancement of healthcare.
 
• IMA actively advocates for the rights and welfare of doctors, engages in healthcare policy discussions, and seeks to bring about reforms in the healthcare system.
 
 
 
• **NITI Ayog**
 
 
• NITI Aayog, short for **National Institution for Transforming India**, is a **policy think tank and a government institution **in India.
 
• It was **established on January 1, 2015**, replacing the previous Planning Commission.
 
• It operates under the guidance and leadership of the **Prime Minister of India.**
 
• NITI Aayog has launched several important initiatives such as **Atal Innovation Mission, Sustainable Development Goals (SDG) India Index, and National Health Stack, **to name a few. These initiatives aim to promote innovation, sustainable development, and improve governance across various sectors.

questions.question: What is the full form of URL?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Uniform Resource Locator**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The full form of the **URL** is **Uniform Resource Locator**.
 
• URL serves as a web address that identifies the **location of a specific resource on the internet**, such as a **web page, image, or document.**
 
• A URL consists of different components, including the **protocol **(such as "http://" or "https://"), the **domain name**, and the **path to the specific resource**.
 
• By using a URL, users can **access and retrieve web content **by entering the URL in a web browser, enabling seamless navigation and retrieval of information on the internet.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Some other Important full forms are as follows:
 
 
• **RAM:** Random Access Memory
 
• **ROM:** Read-Only Memory
 
• **CPU:** Central Processing Unit
 
• **GPU:** Graphics Processing Unit
 
• **BIOS:** Basic Input/Output System
 
• **LAN: **Local Area Network
 
• **WAN: **Wide Area Network
 
• **USB: **Universal Serial Bus
 
• **HDMI: **High-Definition Multimedia Interface
 
• **SSD: **Solid State Drive

questions.question: Which of the following shortcut key is used to move the cursor one word to the left in MS-Word 365?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ctrl + Left arrow key.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ctrl + Left arrow** key is the shortcut key that can be used to **move the cursor one word to the left** in MS Word 365.
 
• This shortcut key** enables the cursor to jump from one word to another towards the left side** of the current cursor position, facilitating easy editing and formatting.
 
• The Ctrl + Left Arrow shortcut key is a commonly used feature in various word processing applications, including MS Word 365, making it a valuable skill for improving productivity across different software platforms.
 
• In the same way, by using **Ctrl + Right Arrow**, you can swiftly **move the cursor to the beginning of the next word on the right side of the current cursor position** in your MS Word 365 document.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Shift + Left arrow key**

 
 
• By **holding down the Shift key and pressing the Left Arrow key**, you can **extend the selection of text to the left of the current cursor position** in your MS Word 365 document.
 
• This shortcut key allows for precise and efficient selection of text by word or character, depending on the number of times the "Left Arrow" key is pressed while holding down "Shift."
 
• Instead of manually clicking and dragging to select text, Shift + Left Arrow provides a faster way to highlight text, saving time and effort, especially when working with large amounts of text.
 
 
 
• **Shift + PageUp**
 
 
• **By holding down the Shift key and pressing the PageUp key**, you can** extend the selection of text upward by one page from the current cursor position** in your MS Word 365 document.
 
• This shortcut key allows for the efficient selection of larger portions of text spanning multiple pages, making it easier to edit, format, or copy and paste content.
 
• Shift + PageUp helps in navigating and selecting text rapidly, especially when you need to work with significant portions of text that are spread across multiple pages.
 
 
 
• **Ctrl + PageUp**
 
 
• **By pressing Ctrl + PageUp**, you can **quickly switch to the previous tab or document page** in your MS Word 365 application.
 
• This shortcut key is especially useful when working with multiple tabs or documents simultaneously, allowing you to easily navigate between them without the need for manual clicking or scrolling.
 
• It enhances productivity by providing a quick way to switch between different sections or content within your MS Word 365 application, improving your overall workflow and task management.

questions.question: Which of the following was the capital of Pandyas?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Madurai.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pandyas**:-

 
 
• The Pandya dynasty was a dynasty of ancient India.
 
• It ruled India from 560 to 1300 AD.
 
• His kingdom was spread over the districts of Mriduraramnad (Madurai in present) and Trinevali.
 
• Their capital was Madura, which in the Tamil language refers to Mathura.
 
• It is also said on the basis of legend that the Pandya rulers were the children of Kuruvanshi and the Pandavas of Mahabharata.
 
• The first mention of the Pandyas was made by Megasthenes in his work Indika.
 
• According to him, women ruled in the Pandya country.
 
 
 
• **Madurai**:-
 
 
• Madura, the later capital of Pandyas was the central seat of Tamil Sangam literature.
 
• Today, Madurai is one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities.
 
• Madurai was located on the banks of River Vaigai in Tamil Nadu.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Puhar:-

 
 
• It is a town in the Nagapattinam district of Tamil Nadu.
 
• It was once a flourishing ancient port city known as Kaveri poompattinam. 
 
• It is mentioned in the Periplus of the Erythraean Sea.
 
• Tamil and Buddhist literature also have references to Poompuhar, or Puhar, as being the port capital of the Chola dynasty.
 
• The ancient Tamil poem Manimekalai by the poet Seethalai Saathanar is set in the town of Kaveripattanam.
 
 
 
• **Aihole**:-
 
 
• Aihole in Karnataka was the **first capital of Chalukyas** where they built numerous temples dating back to the 6th century CE.
 
• Many inscriptions found at Aihole, but the inscription found at Meguti Temple popularly known as Aihole inscription.
 
• The Aihole inscription was written by the Ravikirti, court poet of Chalukya King, Pulakeshi II who reigned from 610 to 642 CE.
 
 
 
• **Kaveripattinam**:​​-
 
 
• ​It is another name for the port city Puhar mentioned above.

• The coastline of the Atlantic Ocean is highly indented.
 
• This irregular and indented coastline provide an ideal location for natural harbours and ports.
 
• From the point of view of commerce, it is the busiest Ocean.
 
 
 
• 
 
Indian Ocean:

 
 
• The Indian Ocean is the only ocean named after a country, that is, India.
 
• The shape of the ocean is almost triangular.
 
• In the north, it is bound by Asia, in the west by Africa and in the east by Australia.
 
• The Southern Ocean encircles the continent of Antarctica and extends northward to 60 degrees south latitude.
 
 
 
• Arctic Ocean:
 
 
• ​The Arctic Ocean is located within the Arctic Circle and surrounds the North Pole.
 
• It is connected with the Pacific Ocean by a narrow stretch of shallow water known as Berring strait.

• International Union for Conservation of Nature:

 
 
• IUCN is a membership Union uniquely composed of both government and civil society organizations.

• It is headquartered in Switzerland.
 
• The IUCN Red List of Threatened Species is the world's most comprehensive inventory of the global conservation status of plant and animal species.
 
• It uses a set of quantitative criteria to evaluate the extinction risk of species. These criteria are relevant to most species and all regions of the world.
 
• The IUCN Red List Categories define the extinction risk of species assessed. 
 
 
• Nine categories extend from NE (Not Evaluated) to EX (Extinct). Critically Endangered (CR), Endangered (EN), and Vulnerable (VU) species are considered to be threatened with extinction.
 
 
 
• It is recognized as the most authoritative guide to the status of biological diversity.
 
• The first international red data books were published in 1966.
 
• ​International Union for Conservation of Nature is founded on 5th October 1948.
 
 
 
• **Asiatic buffalo​**
 
 
• The Asian buffalo, also known as the wild Asian buffalo and the Asiatic buffalo.
 
• It is a giant bovine that is indigenous to Southeast Asia and the Indian subcontinent.
 
• Asia's tropical and subtropical jungles are home to water buffalo.
 
• Since they spend most of their time in the water, their comment is perfect.

questions.question: Provisions as to disqualification on ground of defection are mentioned under which schedule of the Indian constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the __**10th schedule.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__​**

__
 
• **10th schedule:-****​**

 
 
• It includes provisions relating to the disqualification of the members of Parliament and State Legislatures on the ground of defection.
 
• This schedule was added by the 52nd Amendment Act of 1985, also known as the Anti-defection Law. 
 
• The Tenth Schedule of the Constitution is designed to prevent the evil or mischief of political defections motivated by the lure of office or material benefits or other similar considerations.
 
• It is intended to strengthen the fabric of Indian parliamentary democracy by curbing unprincipled and unethical political defections.
 
 
 
• **Grounds for disqualification:-**
 
 
• If an elected member gives up his membership in a political party voluntarily.
 
• If he votes or abstains from voting in the House, contrary to any direction issued by his political party.
 
• If any member who is independently elected joins any party.
 
• If any nominated member joins any political party after the end of 6 months.
 
• The decision on disqualification questions on the ground of defection is referred to the Speaker or the Chairman of the House, and his/her decision is final.
 
• All proceedings in relation to disqualification under this Schedule are considered to be proceedings in Parliament or the Legislature of a state as is the case.
 
 
 
• **​Exceptions Under the Anti-Defection Law:-**
 
 
• In a situation **where two-thirds of the legislators of a political party decide to merge into another party, neither the members who decide to join nor the ones who stay with the original party will face disqualification. **
 
• Any **person elected as chairman or speaker can resign from his party, and rejoin the party if he demits that post. **
 
• Earlier, the law allowed parties to be split, but at present, this has been outlawed.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 
 
Ninth Schedule

 
 
 
It deals with the state acts and regulations that deal with land reforms and

 
abolition of the zamindari system. It also deals with the acts and regulations of the Parliament dealing with other matters.

 
Note: 1st Amendment Act 1951 added the Ninth Schedule to protect the laws included in it from judicial scrutiny on the ground of violation of fundamental rights.

 
However, in 2007, the Supreme Court ruled that the laws included in this schedule after

 
April 24, 1973, are now open to judicial review

 
 
 

 
 
Eleventh Schedule

 
 
 
It contains the provisions that specify the powers, authority, and responsibilities of Panchayats. It has 29 matters.

 
Note: This schedule was added by the 73rd Amendment Act of 1992

 
 
 

 
 
Twelfth Schedule

 
 
 
It deals with the provisions that specify the powers, authority, and responsibilities of Municipalities. It has 18 matters.

 
Note: This schedule was added by the 74th Amendment Act of 1992

questions.question: Which of the following is an exogenic force?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Wind.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Exogenic force:-****​**

 
 
• ​Exogenic forces, often known as external forces, are those that originate in the earth's atmosphere or get their energy from the outside of the planet.
 
• While pressure that arises from within the earth is referred to as endogenic forces, also known as internal forces.
 
• Denudation, which means to strip off or uncover, is a broad term used to describe all exogenic processes.
 
• Geomorphic agents are the parts of nature that can carry out these exogenic processes (or exogenic geomorphic agents). the waves, water, wind, etc. **(Hence option 3 is correct)**
 
 
 
• **Wind:-**
 
 
• The movement of air from high-pressure areas to low-pressure areas is called wind.
 
• There are three kinds of winds including permanent, seasonal, and local winds.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **L**andslide:-

 
 
• A landslide is the movement of rock, earth, or debris down a sloped section of land. 
 
• Landslides are caused by rain, earthquakes, volcanoes, or other factors that make the slope unstable. 
 
 
 
• **Earthquake****​:-****​**
 
 
• A sudden shaking of the ground causes greater destruction to human life and is termed an earthquake.
 
 
 
• **Volcano:- ** 
 
 
• A Volcano is basically an opening in the Earth’s crust through which heated, materials usually in the form of magma are ejected out to the surface of Earth.
